entries.text: First, a program should not require its readers to hold

reading_layout.source_text: First, a program should not require its readers to hold more than a handful of facts in memory at once (1a). Human working memory can hold only a handful of items at a time, where each item is either a single fact or a "chunk" aggregating several facts [33,34], so programs should limit the total number of items to be remembered to accomplish a task. The primary way to accomplish this is to break programs up into easily understood functions, each of which conducts a single, easily understood, task. This serves to make each piece of the program easier to understand in the same way that breaking up a scientific paper using sections and paragraphs makes it easier to read.

entries.text: Science often involves repetition of computational tasks such as

reading_layout.source_text: Science often involves repetition of computational tasks such as processing large numbers of data files in the same way or regenerating figures each time new data are added to an existing analysis. Computers were invented to do these kinds of repetitive tasks but, even today, many scientists type the same commands in over and over again or click the same buttons repeatedly [17]. In addition to wasting time, sooner or later even the most careful researcher will lose focus while doing this and make mistakes.

reading_layout.source_text: A file containing commands for an interactive system is often called a script, though there is real no difference between this and a program. When these scripts are repeatedly used in the same way, or in combination, a workflow management tool can be used. The paradigmatic example is compiling and linking programs in languages such as Fortran, C++, Java, and C# [40]. The most widely used tool for this task is probably Make (http://www..gnu.org/software/make), although many alternatives are now available [41]. All of these allow people to express dependencies between files, i.e., to say that if A or B has changed, then C needs to be updated using a specific set of commands. These tools have been successfully adopted for scientific workflows as well [42].

bilingual_translation_units.source_text: Write Programs for People, Not Computers
bilingual_translation_units.translated_text: 为人们撰写程序, 不是计算机

bilingual_translation_units.source_text: Scientists writing software need to write code that both executes correctly and can be easily read and understood by other programmers (especially the author's future self).
bilingual_translation_units.translated_text: 科学家写作软件需要写作代码,既能正确执行,又能容易地被其他程序员(尤其是作者的未来自我)读懂和理解.

bilingual_translation_units.source_text: If software cannot be easily read and understood, it is much more difficult to
bilingual_translation_units.translated_text: 如果软件不易阅读和理解,就更难

bilingual_translation_units.source_text: PLOS Biology www.plosbiology.org
bilingual_translation_units.translated_text: PLOS 生物学 www.plosbiology.org

bilingual_translation_units.source_text: know that it is actually doing what it is intended to do.
bilingual_translation_units.translated_text: 你知道它实际上正在做它打算做的事。

bilingual_translation_units.source_text: To be productive, software developers must therefore take several aspects of human cognition into account: in particular, that human working memory is limited, human pattern matching abilities are finely tuned, and human attention span is short [33 37].
bilingual_translation_units.translated_text: 因此,软件开发者要取得成效,必须考虑到人类认知的几个方面:特别是人类工作记忆有限,人类模式匹配能力得到精细调整,人类注意力跨度较短[33,37].

bilingual_translation_units.source_text: First, a program should not require its readers to hold more than a handful of facts in memory at once (1a).
bilingual_translation_units.translated_text: 首先,一个程序不应要求其读者同时持有多于少数的记忆事实(1a).

bilingual_translation_units.source_text: Human working memory can hold only a handful of items at a time, where each item is either a single fact or a "chunk" aggregating several facts [33,34], so programs should limit the total number of items to be remembered to accomplish a task.
bilingual_translation_units.translated_text: 人类的工作记忆每次只能持有少数物品,每个物品要么是一个单一的事实,要么是一个"cunk",集合了几种事实[33,34],因此程序应该限制要记住的物品总数来完成一个任务.

bilingual_translation_units.source_text: The primary way to accomplish this is to break programs up into easily understood functions, each of which conducts a single, easily understood, task.
bilingual_translation_units.translated_text: 做到这一点的主要方法是将程序分解为易于理解的功能,每个功能都执行一个单一的,易于理解的任务.

bilingual_translation_units.source_text: This serves to make each piece of the program easier to understand in the same way that breaking up a scientific paper using sections and paragraphs makes it easier to read.
bilingual_translation_units.translated_text: 这使得程序的每一部分都更容易以同样的方式理解,用段落和段落拆散一份科学论文就更容易阅读.

bilingual_translation_units.source_text: Second, scientists should make names consistent, distinctive, and meaningful (1b).
bilingual_translation_units.translated_text: 第二,科学家应使名称一致、独特和有意义(1b)。

bilingual_translation_units.source_text: For example, using non-descriptive names, like a and foo, or names that are very similar, like results and results2, is likely to cause confusion.
bilingual_translation_units.translated_text: 例如,使用非描述性名称,如a和foo,或非常相似的名称,如结果和结果2,很可能导致混乱.

bilingual_translation_units.source_text: Third, scientists should make code style and formatting consistent (1c).
bilingual_translation_units.translated_text: 第三,科学家应使代码样式和格式一致(1c)。

bilingual_translation_units.source_text: If different parts of a scientific paper used different formatting and capitalization, it would make that paper more difficult to read.
bilingual_translation_units.translated_text: 如果科学论文的不同部分采用不同的格式和资本化,将使该文件更难阅读。

bilingual_translation_units.source_text: Likewise, if different parts of a program are indented differently, or if programmers mix CamelCaseNaming and pothole_ case_ naming, code takes longer to read and readers make more mistakes [35,36].
bilingual_translation_units.translated_text: 同样,如果一个程序的不同部分有不同的缩进,或者如果程序员混合了CamelCaseNaming和pothole case 命名,代码需要更长的时间来读取,读者会犯更多的错误[35,36].

bilingual_translation_units.source_text: Let the Computer Do the Work
bilingual_translation_units.translated_text: 让计算机做工作

bilingual_translation_units.source_text: Science often involves repetition of computational tasks such as processing large numbers of data files in the same way or regenerating figures each time new data are added to an existing analysis.
bilingual_translation_units.translated_text: 科学往往涉及重复计算任务,如以同样的方式处理大量数据文件,或每次在现有分析中添加新数据时重生成数字.

bilingual_translation_units.source_text: Computers were invented to do these kinds of repetitive tasks but, even today, many scientists type the same commands in over and over again or click the same buttons repeatedly [17].
bilingual_translation_units.translated_text: 计算机被发明来完成这种重复的任务,但即使在今天,许多科学家反复地输入相同的命令,或者反复点击相同的按钮[17].

bilingual_translation_units.source_text: In addition to wasting time, sooner or later even the most careful researcher will lose focus while doing this and make mistakes.
bilingual_translation_units.translated_text: 除了浪费时间之外,即使最谨慎的研究人员迟早也会在这样做时失去注意力,犯错误。

bilingual_translation_units.source_text: Scientists should therefore make the computer repeat tasks (2a) and save recent commands in a file for re-use (2b).
bilingual_translation_units.translated_text: 因此,科学家应该使计算机重复任务(2a),并将最近的命令保存在一个文件中,以供重新使用(2b)。

bilingual_translation_units.source_text: For example, most command-line tools have a "history" option that lets users display and re-execute recent commands, with minor edits to filenames or parameters.
bilingual_translation_units.translated_text: 例如,大多数命令行工具都有一个"历史"选项,让用户显示并重新执行最近的命令,小编辑为文件名或参数.

bilingual_translation_units.source_text: This is often cited as one reason command--line interfaces remain popular [38,39]: "do this again" saves time and reduces errors.
bilingual_translation_units.translated_text: 这经常被引用为一个理由命令-线接口仍然流行[38,39]:"再做一次"可以节省时间,减少错误.

bilingual_translation_units.source_text: A file containing commands for an interactive system is often called a script, though there is real no difference between this and a program.
bilingual_translation_units.translated_text: 包含一个交互式系统的命令的文件通常被称为脚本,尽管这与一个程序之间实际上没有区别.

bilingual_translation_units.source_text: When these scripts are repeatedly used in the same way, or in combination, a workflow management tool can be used.
bilingual_translation_units.translated_text: 当这些脚本以同样的方式或组合方式反复使用时,可以使用一个工作流程管理工具.

bilingual_translation_units.source_text: The paradigmatic example is compiling and linking programs in languages such as Fortran, C++, Java, and C# [40].
bilingual_translation_units.translated_text: 这个范式例子正在用福特兰,C++,Java,和C#[40]等语言编译和链接程序.

bilingual_translation_units.source_text: The most widely used tool for this task is probably Make (http://www.
bilingual_translation_units.translated_text: 这项工作最广泛使用的工具可能是Make(http://www.

bilingual_translation_units.source_text: gnu.org/software/make), although many alternatives are now available [41].
bilingual_translation_units.translated_text: gnu.org/software/make),虽然现在有许多替代品可用[41].

bilingual_translation_units.source_text: All of these allow people to express dependencies between files, i.e., to say that if A or B has changed, then C needs to be updated using a specific set of commands.
bilingual_translation_units.translated_text: 所有这些允许人们在文件之间表达依赖关系,也就是说,如果A或B已经改变,那么C就需要使用特定的一组命令来更新.

bilingual_translation_units.source_text: These tools have been successfully adopted for scientific workflows as well [42].
bilingual_translation_units.translated_text: 这些工具也被成功用于科学工作流程[42]。

bilingual_translation_units.source_text: To avoid errors and inefficiencies from repeating commands manually, we recommend that scientists use a build tool to automate workflows (2c), e.g., specify the ways in which intermediate data files and final results depend on each other, and on the programs that create them, so that a single command will regenerate anything that needs to be regenerated.
bilingual_translation_units.translated_text: 为了避免手动重复命令的错误和低效,我们建议科学家使用构建工具实现工作流程自动化(2c),例如,指定中间数据文件和最终结果依赖于彼此的方式,以及创建它们的程序,这样一个单一的命令就可以重新生成任何需要再生成的东西.

To avoid errors and inefficiencies from repeating commands
manually, we recommend that scientists use a build tool to
automate workflows (2c), e.g., specify the ways in which
intermediate data files and final results depend on each other, and
on the programs that create them, so that a single command will
regenerate anything that needs to be regenerated.
